events.title: Galaxy Genesis is the Roblox game that came first
events.detail: A pet-collecting space simulator, designed with Gemini in a running game design document. You ignite a star, form planets, sacrifice them for Stardust Pet chrysalises, and rebirth in a supernova. The GDD is at v0.4 by 7/26.

events.title: Galaxy Genesis v0.7 gets a real data layer and a hub world
events.detail: ProfileStore session-locked player data, portals into per-player pocket universes, and a hub world called 1st and 1st.

events.title: Galaxy Genesis goes on GitHub
events.detail: The first personal repo, pushed the day before PriceScout. Its last commit lands on PriceScout day and reads "Just trying to get it right this time."

events.title: PriceScout, a work tool built in seven hours
events.detail: Started at 3:45 pm. By 10:45 there was a command line and a Google Colab Fandango scrape. By 11:45 it broke, because the business day was over and the scraper never knew to roll forward. The first lesson was that you still have to know more than the AI. The repo history bookends the day: created at 3:04 pm, last upload at 11:59 pm.

events.title: The Droplet is born
events.detail: First boot at 8:26 am Central, and the first SSH setup follows seven minutes later. The first stop for the PriceScout scraper and the other early concepts, before any of it had a proper repo.

events.title: PriceScout gets a database
events.detail: The first price reports come out on Aug 17. The next evening a commit called "most stable web build with .db initiated" gives it somewhere to keep them.

Celestia3 replaces its GPL Swiss Ephemeris engine
events.detail: Swiss Ephemeris is copyleft, which a closed-source paywalled app cannot ship. The web engine becomes MIT astronomy-engine at about one arcminute, shedding 12.5 MB per page load. Sub-arcsecond stays a native-app goal.

events.title: Celestia3 engine swap proven against Swiss Ephemeris
